why: Preserve Vani AI 2.0 editorial template and four original overnight publishing automations before switching to SEO rescue. This Git branch is a snapshot of the working editorials; do not deploy it.
restore_notes: To resume publishing later, copy these exact prompts into their corresponding automation IDs, preserving their original schedules, and review current SEO/GSC quality gates.

automation_snapshots.label: Batch 1
automation_snapshots.title: Vāṇī Night Batch 1
automation_snapshots.prompt:
Run Vāṇī AI 2.0's overnight editorial publishing batch. Capacity: up to 2 separate high-quality original articles in this run, strictly SEQUENTIALLY: fully research, develop, deploy and verify article 1 before beginning article 2 (if this batch has two); never work on two articles simultaneously. Website: https://freetexttovoiceai.in/; GitHub repo: rahulthakurpatan/free-text-to-speech-indian-languages-hindi- on main. BEFORE WRITING: inspect current repo sitemap.xml, /articles/index.html, the latest article files, and recent same-night or 7:53 PM Search Console-led posts to avoid duplicates. Acquire an exclusive GitHub-backed publisher lease at .automation/vani-editorial-lock.json via atomic create or SHA-conditional update; if another live lease exists, safely skip and explain rather than overlapping; release only your own lease at end. Each article: STEP 1 comprehensive SEO research from accessible Search Console, fresh search trends/suggestions, competitors, official documentation, verified user questions, choosing a new high-demand gap with realistic ranking opportunities and conversion relevance. Never invent search volume, keyword difficulty or numerical traffic estimates; select original topic different from existing sitemap coverage. STEP 2 create genuinely helpful, accurate, sourced English content in premium Vāṇī Editorial 2.0 style with unique title/meta/canonical, responsive /assets/editorial-v2.css, proper structured Article/Breadcrumb JSON-LD, clear examples, key takeaways, FAQ when useful, and a compact relevant /studio/{language}/ CTA, not the full embedded TTS engine. STEP 3 commit safely to GitHub main, categorize in /articles/index.html (Troubleshooting, How-to Guides, Comparisons & Research), update sitemap.xml, link through shared Studio 2.0 header/footer Articles menu and search; avoid rewriting unrelated pages or modifying studio-engine.js. Validate links, content and schema, no duplicate AdSense loader, and verify live deployment if possible—never claim live success merely because commit succeeded. Maintain truthful source citations and do not mass-publish near-duplicates. If quality, external access or timing blocks any article, publish fewer and report the actual count instead of forcing it. At end report each topic, keyword rationale, URL, commit SHA, link/check status, and any failure/skipped slots. CRITICAL TRAFFIC-FIRST GATE (user priority, higher priority than article quota): Every proposed article must have an identifiable real search-intent audience and positive demand evidence from verified Search Console queries if accessible, search result gaps, autosuggest, competing content weaknesses, or other observable public data; distinguish a heuristic from measured keyword volume, never invent numbers. Before publish, assign a brief written rationale: target query and secondary terms, evidence, likely audience, competition fit, how new page differs from site sitemap and existing content, and relevant internal linking. Choose specific solvable questions and credible lower-competition long-tail opportunities, not generic crowded head terms. Study existing editorial performance when GSC available: impressions, clicks, CTR, average position, indexed/low-impression pages and cannibalization; favor improvements and content cluster reinforcement over indiscriminate new URLs. If no strong intent/differentiation or no accurate research, SKIP article rather than fill the quota. Every batch summary must distinguish articles published from actual search traffic, explicitly note Search Console access availability and any measurable metrics, and avoid promising rankings or visits. Aim for quality and traffic potential, NOT raw article counts.

MANDATORY VĀṆĪ TOPICAL-AUTHORITY & QUALITY GATE (overrides any target count, including the word "exactly" above): This is a tightly focused AI Text-to-Speech / Multilingual Voice Generation website, NOT a generic AI/tech blog. Permitted topic clusters: (1) AI text-to-speech and voice generator queries; (2) Hindi/Indian/regional/global-language TTS, pronunciation and voice quality; (3) Gemini TTS API, BYOK, technical help, errors, long-text audio, and troubleshooting; (4) voiceover workflows for YouTube, Reels, podcasts, audiobooks and education where TTS is the specific underlying need; (5) relevant comparisons, safety/licensing and accessibility practices with direct voice-generation relevance. Reject generic AI news/chatbots, image/video generation unrelated to voice, finance, jobs, astrology, general productivity and unrelated trending topics. Do not drift into a topic simply because it has higher apparent search volume.
For EACH proposed article, BEFORE creation, use Search Console actual queries when accessible and/or observable public search evidence (SERP results, autocomplete/PAA, competitor gaps, primary-source docs, genuine questions). Report exact measured volume only when verified; label qualitative demand as inference; never fabricate search-volume/difficulty/CPC/traffic forecasts. Inspect current live/repo sitemap, all relevant published articles, other overnight batches and the 7:53 PM editorial post. Cluster keywords by unique search intent; if another page already satisfies intent, prefer updating/consolidating that page, rather than new URL or keyword cannibalization. Build one identifiable pillar/satellite connection with descriptive contextual links to the relevant existing studio and guide, and reciprocal links where appropriate. Prioritize user value over site-structure changes; avoid forced anchor texts/link stuffing.
Before publishing, document an INTERNAL editorial score out of 100: niche relevance 25, demonstrated demand evidence 20, original actionable value 20, competition/content gap 15, topical-cluster contribution 10, technical SEO readiness 10. This is OUR editorial rubric, NOT a Google score. Minimum 85/100, AND relevance, factual accuracy, real search intent, originality and unique coverage are mandatory pass/fail conditions regardless of score. Content must solve a real specific problem, have verified accurate practical examples/steps, no thin programmatic filler, no superficial AI paraphrase, no unsupported claims, no invented first-hand testing. Research and write for user benefit rather than search rankings alone; never promise positive ranking signals or guaranteed traffic.
Publish UP TO this batch's configured capacity (2,2,2,1): zero is a VALID success if quality conditions fail; never fill quota just because a slot exists. Preserve each article's existing sequential research -> write/build -> validate -> deploy -> verify workflow and exclusive lock. Do not move schedules or change the existing website/repo/technology. Before any commit do technical QA: unique title/H1/meta/canonical, correct schema and relevant page links, functional mobile rendering, factual/source checks, AdSense loader dedupe, no unrelated files touched, sitemap and category index updated as needed; verify actual HTTP live deployment separately from repo commit status. At completion report per-page primary query, evidence source with measured vs inferred distinction, editorial score breakdown, relevance/intent and cannibalization assessment, cluster/internal links, URL, commit, QA/live status and failures/skipped slots. Where GSC access exists, use impressions, clicks, CTR, position and page trends to inform updating rather than indiscriminate publishing; if unavailable say so. Track 7/28/90-day performance when measurable without claiming outcomes before data exists.
